title: SaaS: Repair Subscription Access After Delayed Updates
businessContext: A reporting SaaS restores export access from an old billing update after a cancellation. A separate expiry bug lets trial accounts keep exporting indefinitely.
problemStatement: Implement solution({ state, snapshots, now }) returning { state, canExport, outcomes }. state is the current valid subscription { tenantId, version, status, plan, periodEnd, cancelAtPeriodEnd }. Each snapshot has the same fields. version is a positive integer assigned by our serialized internal reconciler, NOT a Stripe event timestamp or provider version. now and periodEnd use integer epoch seconds. Process snapshots in order, then compute export access from the final state.
constraints: Check tenant first: a different tenant returns mismatch. Invalid fields return invalid: version positive safe integer, periodEnd nonnegative safe integer, cancelAtPeriodEnd boolean, plan starter/pro, status active/trialing/past_due/canceled/unpaid/incomplete. Then version <= current version returns stale; otherwise replace state and return applied.

Export requires plan pro, status active or trialing, and now < periodEnd. An active subscription with cancelAtPeriodEnd true retains access until periodEnd. No grace period is configured. Do not mutate inputs; current state and now are valid.
candidateTasks: Implement ordered snapshot reconciliation and the explicit entitlement policy.
Explain how reconciliation obtains fresh authoritative provider state without inventing ordering guarantees.

testCases.name: Stale and replayed snapshots cannot restore canceled access
Cancellation scheduled for period end preserves current access
Past due does not grant an implicit grace period
Invalid internal version is not applied

hints: Event arrival time does not establish provider state order. This fixture explicitly supplies internal reconciler versions.
Apply validated newer snapshots first; evaluate access using both billing state and the supplied time.
alternativeApproaches: Use provider entitlement APIs behind a cached server-side policy, with explicit cache expiry and a documented outage policy.
commonMistakes: Using event.created as a guaranteed per-subscription sequence.
Revoking access immediately when cancelAtPeriodEnd becomes true.
